issues.description: Backslash-separator traversal (e.g. `foo\..\WEB-INF\web.xml`) is not covered: forFile() splits only on '/', so backslashes survive into resource.getPath() and the forward-slash illegal regex won't match, allowing bypass on Windows servlet containers via getRealPath. This is precisely the variant the official fix (`relativePath.replace('\','/')`) closes.

Mitigation is a denylist regex over normalized paths rather than the CWE-022 defense-of-record (canonicalize then verify containment within an allowed base), making it fragile to future separator/encoding variants.

result.root_cause: The WEB-INF/META-INF/.tml denylist regex is applied to the raw request path before AbstractResource.forFile() canonicalizes '..' segments, so a path that normalizes into a protected folder passes the check and is then streamed.
result.summary: Our patch correctly re-runs the illegal denylist against the fully normalized resource.getPath() after forFile(), which closes the forward-slash '..' traversal class (the POSIX-exploitable POV) at the right conceptual point with a minimal, regression-safe change. However, it takes a different approach from the official fix (a handler-level denylist re-check vs. separator normalization inside forFile) and does not normalize backslashes, so the Windows backslash-separator bypass the official commit specifically targets remains open. It is a valid, well-scoped fix for the tested platform but not a complete superset of the reference fix.
